Hugo Boss Names Frasers' Michael Murray as Supervisory Board Chairman
By Adria Calatayud
Hugo Boss said it appointed Michael Murray, Frasers Group's chief executive, as the next chairman of its supervisory board, weeks after the U.K. retailer achieved a near-majority ownership.
Murray, who has sat on Hugo Boss's supervisory board since May 2025, will succeed Stephan Sturm as chairman, the German premium apparel company said Wednesday.

Sturm earlier this week said he would step down after the changes in the company's shareholder structure and discussions with Frasers, Hugo Boss's largest shareholder. Frasers said at the beginning of the month that it would review whether to maintain its support for Sturm as it said it aimed to gain majority ownership of Hugo Boss.

Murray said he would work with the supervisory and managing boards to ensure continuity and focus on unlocking Hugo Boss's potential. Hugo Boss Chief Executive Officer  Daniel Grieder said Murray, together with Frasers, shares the managing board's view that the company has significant untapped potential.

The company also said Robert Palmer would join its supervisory board, filling the seat left vacant by Sturm's departure. Palmer has served as director of Frasers Group Financial Services since 2022, and the U.K. retailer said earlier this week that it would seek his appointment to the Hugo Boss supervisory board.
